A1.justification: Both readable 20-page PDFs describe the same concept-resurgence study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision of the experiments and explanatory framework.

before.justification: v1 reports original MACE experiments on Stable Diffusion v1.4, including celebrity/object erasure, subsequent fine-tuning, algorithmic and data-dependent analyses, and retained-concept evaluations.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments involving multiple unlearning algorithms, Stable Diffusion v1.4/v2.1, four erasure domains, and one-dimensional diffusion simulations, including supplementary results in Appendices D–G.

M1.justification: The real-image erasure–fine-tuning pipeline remains, but v2 introduces a separate computational modeling procedure in Section 5: rejection-sampled retraining represents exact or approximate unlearning, followed by score-model fine-tuning with a KL-divergence penalty. This new modeling component is distinct from the additional published algorithms evaluated as comparators.

E1.justification: v2 adds Iron Man copyright erasure, I2P unsafe-content erasure covering hate, self-harm, violence, and harassment, and synthetic Gaussian experiments. Celebrity and CIFAR object domains remain. v1's COCO-5K utility evaluation, CelebA-HQ-Dialog-based similarity study, and out-of-domain fine-tuning scenarios are removed.

E2.justification: v1 experimentally studies MACE alone. v2 Tables 1–2 add ESD, SDD, and UCE alongside MACE in corresponding Stable Diffusion v1.4 comparisons; UCE was previously only discussed. Table 3 additionally reports ESD, SDD, and UCE on Stable Diffusion v2.1, with SDD unsafe-content results excluded because initial unlearning destroys utility.

E3.justification: v2 adds Stable Diffusion v2.1 configurations and Molmo/Q16 evaluation protocols for the new tasks. Object evaluation changes from separate automobile, ship, bird, and five-object subtasks to a primary three-object task with one/three/five-object scaling. The toy experiment introduces likelihood evaluation at five points and concept counts among 10,000 generated samples.

E4.justification: MACE scaling analysis is retained and extended to other algorithms. v2 adds ESD unlearning-parameter and UCE fine-tuning-parameter comparisons, plus controlled toy analyses of residual concept probability. It removes v1's mapping-concept, regularization, CLIP-distance, out-of-domain, and quantitative retained-concept/COCO analyses rather than relocating them.

E5.justification: The existing celebrity/object evaluations retain three-seed reporting and error bars. v2 Appendix B newly specifies five generation seeds for copyright evaluation, although their relationship to Section 3's three-seed evaluation is unexplained. Tables 1–4 provide numerical uncertainty summaries, including undefined parenthesized bounds; neither PDF establishes an increased run count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive cross-algorithm, copyright, unsafe-content, SD2.1, and toy results. For example, Table 1 reports ESD celebrity scores of 0.144 before fine-tuning and 0.950 afterward, versus UCE's 0.001 and 0.004. The MACE 100-celebrity result remains approximately 0.042 to 0.391 from v1 Figure 5; removed analyses also remove their result sets.

T1.justification: v1's formal content centers on the MACE cross-attention objective in Equation 1, which disappears. v2 Section 5 introduces interval-defined concepts, Gaussian distributions, and formalized exact/approximate unlearning, with a likelihood calculation in Appendix G. Neither version supplies a theorem or proof. The new rho endpoint definitions conflict with the stated rejection probability.

C1.justification: The central claim that benign fine-tuning can restore erased concepts remains. However, v2 redefines the headline contributions: v1's mapping-concept/regularization account becomes separate investigations of algorithm-dependent severity, scaling, and a toy explanation of resurgence and its detectability. The abstract also broadens the stated investigation beyond MACE and Stable Diffusion v1.4.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes small parameter changes and fine-tuning-data relatedness; v2 emphasizes closed-form versus gradient-based erasure, cross-attention localization, and diffusion models' possible bias toward smooth distributions. It adds utility-related exclusions and qualifications about the toy model. Section 4.1 also changes MACE scaling from increasing resurgence to claimed insensitivity, although Figure 10 still shows an increasing celebrity trend.

D1.justification: v2 Appendices B–C add copyright prompts, retained/fine-tuning character lists, and I2P filtering instructions, including the 0% Q16 criterion for fine-tuning data. Appendix G specifies autograd and 2,000 integration steps. Conversely, v1's detailed CLIP-similarity dataset construction and concept tables disappear. Neither version provides comprehensive training hyperparameters or a project-code access statement.

R1.justification: The positioning expands from a MACE-centered investigation to a comparison of fine-tuning, closed-form, and hybrid erasure approaches. v2 adds references concerning ESD, SDD, other erasure methods, Molmo, unsafe-content evaluation, and diffusion smoothness/likelihood. References supporting the removed artistic-style discussion and data-dependent analyses are dropped; these are substantive literature changes beyond bibliography formatting.

P1.justification: The contribution list and related-work narrative are substantially recast. Section 4 is reorganized around scaling and algorithm choices, while the former data-dependent Section 5 is replaced by a structured toy-model investigation. Appendices A–C become A–G with different purposes, although ordinary celebrity/object fine-tuning curation is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is retained and relocated, and some MACE examples/results are reused. Nevertheless, v2 reorganizes qualitative grids around algorithms, redraws scaling plots with standardized axes, introduces comparative Tables 1–4 and toy-distribution figures, and removes the former sensitivity, utility, and dataset-list displays. This substantially changes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 better validates the central phenomenon beyond v1's MACE/SD1.4 setting, while identifying UCE's relative robustness and directly testing copyright and unsafe-content tasks. However, it removes quantitative utility and data-dependent controls. Its new explanatory material also contains conflicting rho definitions and a MACE scaling interpretation inconsistent with Figure 10. The broader empirical support improves the paper, but these losses and inconsistencies limit the overall gain.
